method: discharge from the gauge's expanded shift-adjusted stage-discharge rating (linear interpolation between rating points on gage height); block value is the time-weighted mean discharge over the closed 6 h interval, trapezoidal in time
published_precision_ambiguity_note: MEASURED 2026-07-28, not asserted. Axis tested: the interpolation convention between tabulated rating points. The oracle reads the USGS EXSA table by linear interpolation on gage height; interpolating log-log between the same two bracketing rows is equally defensible for a power-law rating. Result: the spread is EXACTLY ZERO on all 12 blocks, because all 237 sampled gage heights in stage_series.csv land on a tabulated rating point, so no interpolation route is ever exercised. The convention therefore cannot fail correct work here. Tolerances are 0.2% of reference (e.g. 17.624371 cfs on 8812.185417).

power_law_b2_from_recent_measurement.description: fit Q = C*h^2 through the single supplied recent measurement and evaluate it at each reported stage
power_law_b2_from_recent_measurement.note: worst (smallest) separation over all 12 blocks, in tolerance units. NEAREST REAL COMPETITOR: the standard published stage-discharge form Q = C(h-e)^b anchored on a real measurement - what a competent hydrologist without the table actually does, and the route the recall probe showed the model takes unprompted. Not a strawman.

linear_scale_from_recent_measurement.description: scale the single supplied recent measurement linearly in gage height
linear_scale_from_recent_measurement.note: worst (smallest) separation over all 12 blocks, in tolerance units.

report_recent_measurement_throughout.description: report the supplied recent discharge measurement for every block
report_recent_measurement_throughout.note: worst (smallest) separation over all 12 blocks, in tolerance units.

arithmetic_mean_of_samples.description: rate through the correct table but average the samples arithmetically instead of weighting by elapsed time
arithmetic_mean_of_samples.note: V-06 evidence: a defensible alternative reduction convention. It stays inside tolerance on every block, so pinning the trapezoidal rule in the prompt costs the no-skill arm nothing and the reduction step is NOT part of the lever. The lever is the rating table alone.
